title: まい: the negative helper
summary: まい is the negative volitional: it says something is unlikely, or that you firmly will not do it.

blocks.text: **まい** is an old-fashioned negative helper, a cousin of ない. It is a negative **volitional**: where ~よう means "will / let's", ~まい means "will not / surely not". It never changes (no past, no て-form), and it has two common jobs, plus two set patterns.
まい is usually stuck on the end of the dictionary form: 行くまい, 食べるまい. An ichidan verb can also lose its る (見まい), and the two irregulars have extra forms: する → するまい / しまい, 来る → 来るまい / こまい.
This is the most common use. It is the negative partner of でしょう / だろう, and it can attach straight to a verb, which the positive volitional cannot.

blocks.en: There is surely no such story.

blocks.jp: この雨では、彼は来るまい。
blocks.en: In this rain, he will surely not come.

blocks.text: あるまい means the same as ないだろう, and ではあるまい means ではないだろう.
A firm resolution not to do something.

blocks.jp: 買おうか買うまいか迷う。
blocks.en: I can't decide whether to buy it or not.

blocks.jp: 子供ではあるまいし、泣くな。
blocks.en: You are not a child, so don't cry.

blocks.text: The positive and negative volitional together mean "whether or not". Adding し to まい gives "it's not as if ...".

items: まい = negative volitional: **unlikely** or **I will never**.
It does not make a negative invitation: 行くまい does not mean "let's not go".
Set patterns: ～ようか～まいか (whether or not), ～まいし (it's not as if).

questions.instruction: What kind of helper is まい?
questions.note: よう means will / let's; まい means will not.

questions.instruction: How do you attach まい to 飲む?
questions.note: まい goes on the end of the dictionary form.

questions.instruction: Which is the まい form of 見る?
questions.note: An ichidan verb can lose its る: 見まい.

questions.instruction: Which is the まい form of 来る in kana?
questions.note: 来る → 来るまい / こまい.

questions.prompt: この天気では、雪は降るまい。
options: It is unlikely that snow will fall
I will never let it snow
questions.note: The first job of まい: it is unlikely.
questions.en: In this weather, it surely won't snow.

questions.prompt: もう二度と彼には会うまい。
questions.note: The second job of まい: I will never.
questions.en: I will never see him again.

questions.prompt: 行くまい means "let's not go".
questions.note: まい never makes a negative invitation.
questions.en: 行くまい: I won't go.

questions.prompt: まい changes into a past form like ない does.
questions.note: まい never changes: no past, no て-form.
questions.en: まい vs ない: does まい have a past?

questions.instruction: あるまい means the same as...
questions.note: まい is the negative partner of だろう.

questions.instruction: ではあるまい means the same as...
questions.note: あるまい = ないだろう.
まい on the dictionary form says it is unlikely.
questions.en: He surely won't come to school today.

questions.prompt: いいえ、もう二度と食べ＿＿＿。
questions.note: A firm resolution: 食べまい.
questions.en: No, I will never eat it again.

questions.instruction: Which sentence says "whether to go or not"?
options: 行くまいか行くまいか迷う
行こうか行こうか迷う
行こうか行くまいか迷う
行くか行かまいか迷う
questions.note: Positive volitional + negative volitional: ようか～まいか.

questions.prompt: 学生ではあるまいし、毎日遊んではいられない。
options: It's not as if (you are a student)
questions.note: Adding し to まい gives "it's not as if ...".
questions.en: It's not as if you are a student; you can't play every day.

questions.note: まい makes 言う a "surely not / never".
questions.en: I won't say such a thing.

questions.note: まい is the negative helper at the end.
questions.en: On a night like this, surely no one will come.

questions.prompt: I will never be late again.
questions.note: An ichidan verb loses る before まい.
questions.en: I will never be late again.

questions.prompt: He surely won't know such a thing.
questions.note: まい on the dictionary form: unlikely.
questions.en: He surely won't know such a thing.

questions.prompt: I can't decide whether to go or not.
questions.note: ようか～まいか means whether or not.
questions.en: I can't decide whether to go or not.

questions.instruction: Which is the opposite of ~よう (will)?
questions.note: よう is will; まい is will not.

questions.instruction: Which sentence means the same as 彼は行くまい?
questions.note: まい: surely not.
